items.title: Reported minimum O2 vs the boundary fitted from the plotted data
items.detail: Report: ~13.5 % O2 at a = 8-12 1/s. Fit: 13.62 % (90 % band 13.40-13.85 %) at a = 9.9 1/s. The report's value is inside the band.

refs.quote: The minimum in this boundary occurs at a = 8 to 12 s-1 at approximately 13.5 percent O2

items.title: Normal-gravity upward limit (15.4 % O2) vs flames that kept burning in microgravity
items.detail: 24 microgravity flames burned stably below 15.4 % O2 (lowest 13.6 %). A 1g screening limit is not conservative here.

refs.quote: significantly lower than the observed upward flame spread limit of 15.4 percent O2

items.title: Authors' empirical boundary (Eq. 6.1) vs IGNIS fitted boundary
items.detail: Eq. 6.1 lies outside the IGNIS 90 % band on 20 % of the stretch-rate range (max gap 1.20 O2 % points). Same data, different fitting choices (IGNIS also uses the drop-tower points and treats extinctions as boundary measurements).

refs.quote: The O2 concentration (XO2) versus a boundary is defined by the combined empirical equations

items.title: Zero Gravity Research Facility residual gravity: two NASA documents disagree 10x
items.detail: 1999 user's guide: 10^-6 g. 2018 GRC paper: less than 10^-5 g. IGNIS uses the larger (conservative) value as the campaign nominal. Both are far below ISS levels for this model's purpose.

refs.quote: achieves a gravity level of 10 -6 Gs

items.title: Report: drop-tower blowoff agrees with flight blowoff
items.detail: Linear blowoff fits over the shared range a = 47-144 1/s differ by at most 0.42 O2 % points (ISS: 0.0142 a + 13.79; drop tower: 0.0190 a + 13.15).

refs.quote: The drop tower blowoff data, given by the purple dashed line, agrees very well with the flight data.

items.title: 10 pairs of opposite outcomes at nearly the same conditions
items.detail: Stable flame and extinction plotted at (almost) the same stretch rate and O2. All sit on the fitted boundary, where the report says flames are sensitive to stochastic perturbations, so IGNIS keeps both and models the boundary as a band, not a line. ISS stable flame vs ISS quench at a = 1.6 / 1.6 1/s, O2 16.75 / 16.70 %; ISS stable flame vs ISS quench at a = 3.8 / 3.6 1/s, O2 14.61 / 14.60 %; ISS stable flame vs ISS quench at a = 6.4 / 6.3 1/s, O2 14.60 / 14.60 %; ISS stable flame vs ISS blowoff at a = 10.8 / 11.5 1/s, O2 14.50 / 14.50 %; ISS stable flame vs ISS blowoff at a = 25.4 / 25.0 1/s, O2 14.20 / 14.20 %; ISS stable flame vs ISS blowoff at a = 25.4 / 26.8 1/s, O2 14.20 / 14.20 %; ISS stable flame vs ISS blowoff at a = 37.4 / 36.6 1/s, O2 14.50 / 14.50 %; ISS stable flame vs ISS blowoff at a = 51.3 / 53.0 1/s, O2 14.30 / 14.29 %; ISS stable flame vs ISS blowoff at a = 71.9 / 74.3 1/s, O2 14.80 / 14.80 %; Drop Tower blowoff vs Drop Tower stable flame at a = 67.2 / 63.9 1/s, O2 15.00 / 14.99 %.

refs.quote: Along this boundary, the flame is sensitive to stochastic perturbations that can lead to extinguishment

items.title: Report's highest 100-um PMMA spread rate vs re-measurement from NASA's flight stills
items.detail: Report: about 2.2 mm/s. Re-measured from the public PSI top-view stills: highest 4.23 +/- 0.31 mm/s (test B3), scale range 3.21-4.23 mm/s. Status 'tension'. The length scale (flame width = 2 cm sample) is the dominant uncertainty.

refs.quote: For the same fuel thickness, the highest spread rate obtained is about 2.2 mm/s
photographed with a high-resolution digital still camera with a frame rate of 1 per second
